claims.text: OpenTofu plans and applies one configuration at a time: the files of the working directory (here chosen with -chdir) and that configuration's state; a plan works from only these and checks only the real objects that state records.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > Files and Directories (a configuration is the .tf files of one directory, root module); CLI > tofu plan; CLI > Switching working directory with -chdir

claims.text: A workspace is one of several named states for the same configuration directory; every configuration starts in the workspace named default, and tofu workspace select <name> chooses the workspace later plans and applies use.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > State > Workspaces; CLI > tofu workspace select

claims.text: All workspaces of a directory use the same .tf files and the same backend, so they can differ only through values chosen per workspace, such as input variable values; their states are all kept in that one backend.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > State > Workspaces; CLI > Workspaces (multiple instances of a single configuration within its single backend)

claims.text: A data block only reads existing objects, creating none; the terraform_remote_state data source reads another configuration's root-module outputs from its latest state snapshot, referenced as data.terraform_remote_state.<name>.outputs.<output>.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > State > The terraform_remote_state Data Source (only root module outputs; example usage)

claims.text: OpenTofu's documentation says a provider configuration's arguments may reference only values known before the configuration is applied; the cluster's endpoint and certificates are known only after kind_cluster is created.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > Providers > Provider Configuration (values known before apply); outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-environments.txt lines 11-17

claims.text: The Kubernetes provider (hashicorp/kubernetes 3.3) accepts host, cluster_ca_certificate, client_certificate and client_key to connect to the API server; the last three are the credentials a kubeconfig holds for kubectl.
claims.source_hint: search.opentofu.org hashicorp/kubernetes 3.3: provider Argument Reference; kubernetes.io: Organizing cluster access using kubeconfig files (client-certificate-data, client-key-data)

claims.text: At stage-3, envs/staging/cluster/main.tf calls ../../../modules/kind-cluster with name donhang-staging and workers = 0; envs/production/cluster/main.tf calls it with name donhang-production and workers = 2.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/tofu/envs/staging/cluster/main.tf lines 9-22 and envs/production/cluster/main.tf lines 9-13 at stage-3

claims.text: kind-cluster creates one control-plane node plus var.workers worker nodes, so workers = 0 is one node and workers = 2 is a control plane and two workers.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/tofu/modules/kind-cluster/main.tf at stage-3 (header comment; node blocks, dynamic node with range(var.workers))

claims.text: Each deploy/tofu/envs/<env>/<layer> folder has main.tf, backend.tf, .terraform.lock.hcl; backend.tf sets pg with schema_name <env>_<layer> (e.g. staging_cluster) in database donhang_tofu of Compose's PostgreSQL, started by scripts/up.sh; one state per folder.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/tofu/envs/*/*/backend.tf at stage-3 (schema_name, header comment); scripts/devops/tofu-environments.sh header; directory listing

claims.text: staging/platform/main.tf reads the cluster layer's outputs with data "terraform_remote_state" "cluster" (backend pg, schema_name staging_cluster) and sets the Kubernetes provider from them; production also has a platform folder, reading production_cluster.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/tofu/envs/staging/platform/main.tf lines 9-24; envs/production/platform/main.tf lines 9-17 at stage-3

claims.text: Applying staging's platform layer creates the namespace donhang (kubernetes_namespace_v1) and one Secret sealing-key in kube-system: 'Plan: 2 to add' and 'Apply complete! Resources: 2 added'.

tofu-environments.sh applies staging's cluster layer, then staging's platform layer (both -auto-approve), then only plans production's cluster layer and runs kind get clusters, which lists the kind clusters on the machine.

In the captured run, production's plan prints 'module.cluster.kind_cluster.this will be created', name "donhang-production" and 'Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.'; kind get clusters lists donhang and donhang-staging only.

Running the script again: production's plan again proposes 1 to add, since its state records nothing and the script never applies production; staging's applies find their objects already in state and have nothing to create.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > tofu plan (compares state and configuration); tofu-environments.sh never applies production; outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-environments.txt

claims.text: The kind provider creates the cluster in the staging apply when donhang-staging does not exist, waiting for it to be ready (wait_for_ready = true).
claims.source_hint: search.opentofu.org tehcyx/kind 0.11 docs: kind_cluster (wait_for_ready); kind-cluster/main.tf at stage-3

claims.text: Prefer a folder per environment over workspaces when environments must differ in more than values chosen per workspace or must be impossible to apply by mistake from the wrong selection; opposing view: workspaces fit many copies that differ only in values, without repeating module calls.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: Language > State > Workspaces (when to use / not to use workspaces)

claims.text: Đơn Hàng at stage-3 uses no OpenTofu workspaces: each environment and layer is a folder under deploy/tofu/envs.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/tofu and scripts/devops/tofu-*.sh at stage-3 (no tofu workspace command)

claims.text: Separate state keeps production out of staging's plans only while staging's values point at staging's cluster: e.g. schema_name = "production_cluster" in staging's platform folder would connect its provider to production's cluster.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > tofu plan (refresh reads remote objects); Language > Providers > Provider Configuration; staging/platform/main.tf lines 12-24 at stage-3
